report:
**Conclusion: Yes, the weight of evidence supports that broad population mask wearing can reduce SARS-CoV-2 transmission, though the magnitude varies and randomized trial evidence remains limited.**

**Supporting evidence:**
- A 2022 PNAS study estimated that population mask wearing corresponded to a ~19% decrease in SARS-CoV-2 transmission, with larger effects when compliance was high (https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2119266119).
- A 2021 PNAS evidence review concluded that mask wearing reduces transmissibility per contact and is most effective at the population level when compliance is high (https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2014564118).
- A 2025 systematic review in IJERPH found that masking policies and mask wearing were beneficial for preventing or reducing SARS-CoV-2 infection across real-world settings (https://www.mdpi.com/1660-4601/22/10/1590).

**Evidence against / nuance:**
- The 2023 Cochrane review concluded that it is uncertain from randomized controlled trials whether community mask interventions slow respiratory virus spread; results were inconclusive, not proof that masks are ineffective (https://www.cochrane.org/about-us/news/statement-physical-interventions-interrupt-or-reduce-spread-respiratory-viruses-review).

**Summary:** Observational studies, mechanistic evidence, and the large Bangladesh cluster randomized trial support that masks—especially surgical masks—reduce transmission when widely used. However, RCT evidence overall is limited and mixed, so confidence in the size of the population-level effect is moderate rather than definitive.
